unsupported_claims: The model stops preserving second-order proximity when the weight on the second-order term is set to zero or the second-order objective is disabled, so the loss reduces to first-order.
A degenerate case, such as vertices with no shared neighbors, is an alternative condition under which the model focuses only on first-order proximity.
rationale: The answer goes along with the false premise and invents conditions under which the model drops second-order proximity. It never corrects the premise, and the evidence says the model is defined using both first-order and second-order proximities, with no such switch.
